title: Tense Review, Hobbies & Short Answers
subtitle: Review sentence patterns and explain your ideas in two or three sentences.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: A grammar and vocabulary challenge
sections.intro: We reviewed tense choices and sentence structure through a challenge, then revisited hobbies, puzzles, opponents and climbing.

cards.title: Read the meaning first
cards.text: Ask whether a sentence describes a routine, an action happening around now, or a future plan before choosing a form.

cards.title: Notice sense verbs
cards.text: A taste or smell can describe a quality: ‘The pie tastes great.’ A person can also actively taste or smell something: ‘The chef is tasting the sauce.’

cards.title: A short written response
cards.text: For the reading task, answer each question in about two or three sentences. Give your main answer and add a brief explanation.

cards.title: Present continuous
cards.text: Use am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now or around now: ‘The intern is helping in the kitchen today.’ In a question, put be before the subject: ‘What are you doing?’

cards.title: Future plans with going to
cards.text: Use am/is/are + going to + base verb for an intention: ‘I’m going to open the door.’ The be verb changes with the subject: she is, they are.

cards.title: Routines and frequency
cards.text: Use present simple for habits: ‘He often comes to class late.’ Frequency adverbs usually go before the main verb; after be, they come after be.

cards.title: A useful correction
cards.text: Describe a food’s quality with a state verb: ‘The apple pie tastes great’, not usually ‘is tasting great’. Use continuous for an active test: ‘The chef is tasting it.’

cards.title: opponent
cards.text: A person or team you compete against. ‘Her opponent played well.’

cards.title: climbing
cards.text: The activity of moving up a mountain or other steep surface. ‘Climbing a mountain can be a memorable experience.’

cards.title: experience
cards.text: An event or activity that happens to someone. ‘The climb was a new experience.’

cards.title: intern
cards.text: A person gaining practical work experience. ‘The intern is helping the team today.’

cards.title: puzzle
cards.text: A problem or picture made from pieces that you try to solve. ‘They are doing a puzzle.’

cards.title: can't stand
cards.text: Dislike something very strongly. ‘I can’t stand that music.’

activities.prompt: Correct the sentence: The pie is tasting great.
Put the words in order: thinking / what / you / are / about / now?
activities.example: What are you thinking about now?

activities.prompt: Complete with a future intention: I am going to ___ (open) the door.
activities.example: I am going to open the door.

activities.prompt: Write one sentence about a routine and one about something happening around now.
activities.example: I usually do puzzles on Sundays. This week I’m trying a new puzzle.

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: A new activity
sections.intro: For each question, write approximately two or three sentences: answer, then explain briefly.

readings.title: Trying a climbing class
readings.text:
Leo usually spends his free time doing puzzles and playing games. This month, his friend is trying a climbing class and invites him to join. Leo is interested, but he is not sure whether he will enjoy climbing.

The class has beginners and more experienced climbers. There is no opponent: people help one another learn safely. Leo decides he is going to try one class before choosing a regular activity. He thinks a new experience may help him discover what he enjoys.

questions.q: Which activity does Leo decide to try?
What do the people in the class do?
opt: They help one another learn safely.

activities.prompt: Why does Leo want to try the class? Give your answer and a reason in two or three sentences.
activities.example: Leo wants to try climbing because it is a new activity. He hopes the experience will help him discover what he enjoys.

activities.prompt: Would you try a new activity before choosing a regular hobby? Explain in two or three sentences.
activities.example: Yes, I would try a class first. It would help me decide whether the activity suits me.

sections.label: Listening
sections.title: Listen for a plan
sections.intro: Listening was postponed during the lesson. This short optional review uses the same themes; play it or read the script.
sections.audioText: I usually do puzzles after work. This week I'm trying a climbing class with a friend. We are going to start with the beginners because we want to learn safely.

activities.prompt: What does the speaker usually do, and what are they trying this week?
activities.example: The speaker usually does puzzles. This week they are trying a climbing class.

questions.q: Complete: They ___ going to try a class.
Choose the natural description of a pie.

opt: He often comes to class late.
He is going to come tomorrow.
questions.hint: Look for often and present simple.

questions.q: Complete the question: What ___ thinking about?
questions.hint: In a question, be comes before the subject.

questions.q: Which activity involves moving up a mountain?
questions.hint: It can be a physical activity.

questions.q: Choose the sentence about an active test.
opt: The chef is tasting the sauce.
questions.hint: The chef is doing something now.

questions.q: Which sentence shows a future intention?
opt: I'm going to open the door.

questions.q: What is a useful short explanatory answer?
opt: A main answer followed by a brief reason.
A very long essay every time.
